exposure: anti-seizure medication (ASM) use (any, new generation, polytherapy, gabapentin)
cohort: The study included 1,331 pregnant women with epilepsy and 357,334 women without epilepsy in Manitoba, Canada, from 1995 to 2019.
finding: Breastfeeding initiation was approximately 10% lower in women with epilepsy compared to women without epilepsy, with low income, ASM use, and comorbidities being significant contributors to reduced BFI in both groups.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery was associated with a reduced likelihood of breastfeeding initiation among women with epilepsy (aOR=0.72).
gest_age: Gestational age was positively associated with breastfeeding initiation in both women with epilepsy (aOR=1.09) and women without epilepsy (aOR=1.13).
